method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: sheet 11 (north of the corridor) prints '27TH ST.' in the corridor at its bottom margin with the neighbour plate number '13'; its 27th-St north-side evens read '102 104 106 108 110 112' in the Ave A-B block and the Ave B frontage closes with 2625/2626/2627/2628 (the 26th-27th segment). sheet 13 (south) prints '27TH ST.' at its top margin with neighbour '11'; south-side odds read '101 103 105 107 109 111' and the Ave B frontage restarts at 2702/2704/2706/2708 running to 2727/2728 (the 27th-28th segment). One block south the plate prints '28TH ST.' with its own 102-112 / 101-111 and Ave B 2801/2802, so the read line is not 28th. Evens on the north side and odds on the south side interlock one-for-one and the hundred-block changes fall on the avenues named in each key map, so the read line is the shared corridor and not the block-pitch (~1160-1180 px) neighbour street.
note: Reported value is the drafted corridor CENTRELINE in that sheet's own working-raster pixels (work/sheets/1912w/u<N>.jpg, the same pixels the green rulers label), following the pair_33_34 convention. both faces read on sheet 13 (N 99.0 / S 338.6 at x 700-1500, drafted width 239.6); on sheet 11 only the north face is drafted (3639.2, sheet-wide usable mean) and the centre is that face + 120 px = half the drafted 80' width. full A-C overlap; sheet-wide means used. The drafted 80' corridor measures 239-245 px on these plates; centreline sigma ~3 px, plus ~2 px where a half-width had to be supplied. Each plate's frontage tilts 8-13 px across the sheet, so the reading window was matched to the two plates' shared avenue. Detection's candidates were all block-interior or siding lines (e.g. sheet 11 cand1 y=3558 falls inside the Pattern & Casting warehouse, 200 px north of the corridor centre) and none were used.
